paper: Michael G. Pratt (2000), "The Good, the Bad, and the Ambivalent: Managing Identification among Amway Distributors," Administrative Science Quarterly, 45: 456-493

readings.wager: Seekership is brought to Amway, not made by it. Members who identify, for or against, arrive already discontented with their job, money or family situation. Dream building gives that discontent a vocabulary rather than breaking a settled sense of self. Those who drift away are those whose outside lives were, or became, satisfactory. On this reading the first branch of the model sorts people by prior circumstance, not by whether a practice succeeded.

evidence.job: The paper says identity deficits bite hardest on people in crisis or unhappy with who they are. This concedes that prior state conditions the effect.
The success-story distributor credits her upline with carrying her through a divorce. The trouble predates the bond.
Testimonies of an upline helping one member off drugs and feeding a couple in need. Again need precedes attachment.
In Table 1 the family dream is voiced by a man whose wife is worn out by her job and whose child is in day care all week. The dream reads as a description of an existing strain.
An ambivalent distributor frames his dream as escaping a job where others control whether he works. This is a grievance about present employment.
The non-renewer explains leaving by saying her job is now going well and she likes it. Deidentification here follows outside contentment.

The general model adds a selection box and allows that some people are predisposed to seek, through dissatisfaction or disposition. The paper thus names this route itself but does not test it on its own informants.
Footnote 9 admits individual differences cannot be ruled out. The design did not collect what would rule them out.

what_it_would_take_to_cohere.observation: For each informant, an account of work, money and family circumstances at the moment of recruitment, taken before or independently of their Amway career, and set against their eventual identification type. If the positive, negative and ambivalent groups were already dissatisfied on entry and the deidentified were not, the reading holds. The paper prints scattered biographical fragments but no such comparison, and states that individual differences were outside its purpose (p. 457).

strains_against.why: Ken reports he had always got on with his boss and only after joining came to see her in Amway's terms. That is discontent manufactured, not imported.
The author, who joined as a researcher, records being swept up by dreams he also thought foolish. The practice moved someone with no reported prior grievance.
The Emerald says most people do not know what they want and must be taught by example. The organisation's own theory is that wants are instilled.
Distributors are urged to replace each achieved dream with a larger one. Continued seeking among the already successful cannot be prior discontent.

readings.who_could_complete_it: A researcher able to interview prospects at or before sign-up about their current lives and then follow them for a year or more; or intake material such as needs-analysis notes kept by sponsors at recruitment.

readings.wager: There is one practice, not two. The upline relationship does all the work, and dream building is something done inside it. Dreams are supplied, shaped and kept alive by the mentor, so a 'successful' dream is evidence of a working bond and a faded dream is evidence of a bond that never formed or went sour. The paper's two-by-two logic then collapses into a single dimension, the quality of the tie to the upline, with ambivalence as its middle value.

evidence.job: Members learn what to dream mainly by modelling [6 words of Pratt (2000), p. 465] people in their own line. The content of the dream comes from the upline.
Upline and downline jointly craft the individual dream from a finite approved menu. Dream building is described as a relational activity.

In the appendix the Emerald chooses the shops, the colours and the items, and the author likes almost nothing all day. Meanwhile a joking father-son exchange occurs. The session produces a bond more visibly than a want.
A distributor wants to reach Pearl in order to golf with his upline because he likes them. The dream's object is the relationship.
An interviewee says those who stay active are those who keep [7 words of Pratt (2000), p. 475]. This is a member's own single-factor theory.
The disidentified former distributor complains that his upline did not know how to excite him. Failure to kindle the dream and failure of the bond are the same event in his telling.
The deidentified leaver describes growing distance from his sponsors and discomfort with reverence for Diamonds. The case filed under failed sensebreaking carries a relationship story.
The paper acknowledges that the two kinds of tactic blur once sensegiving starts, as the ideal self comes under other distributors' influence.

what_it_would_take_to_cohere.observation: A member observed, at the time and not in recollection, holding a live Amway dream with no working upline tie, or a warm upline tie with no dream. If neither occurs, the practices are not separable. The nearest printed material is the disidentified cases (pp. 478-479). But there the evidence of a dream is a recalled attraction to a recruiter's house and an ambition to practise law that lies outside Amway.

strains_against.why: An inactive distributor describes a warm, unconditional tie to his sponsor yet does not sell, sponsor or attend reliably. A strong bond without the outcome means the bond alone is not sufficient.
The paper locates ambivalence in retained outside ties, not in a weaker upline bond. A single upline dimension has no place for that.
The non-renewer's stated reason is that her job is going well. No upline relationship, good or bad, figures in it.
Dreams also reach members passively through tapes, magazines and slide shows. Some dream building happens without a personal mentor present.

readings.who_could_complete_it: Someone with access to sponsor-recruit pairs from first contact, such as paired interviews or the sponsor's own records of sessions, able to date when the bond formed relative to when the recruit first voiced a dream.

readings.wager: The outcome is decided outside Amway, by how a member's existing circle responds when approached. Where family and friends join or at least tolerate the venture, the member's world fills with supporters and looks encapsulated. Where valued others recoil and the member is unwilling to lose them, the member hedges, hides and stalls. Where the member's confidants are hostile, the member turns against the organisation. Encapsulation is then something outsiders do to distributors as much as something positive programming does to members.

evidence.job: Non-members told the author they avoid distributor friends and relatives, and a distributor calls the first months the hardest because of how intimates react. The barrier is built from both sides.
Bringing family and friends in is said to secure [6 words of Pratt (2000), p. 473]. Who says yes determines the member's surroundings.
A friend schedules his wedding against an Amway event, and unsupportive spouses are a named category needing continued persuasion. Outsiders are active parties.
One ambivalent distributor [6 words of Pratt (2000), p. 480]. Another disowns Amway on the spot when a co-worker repeats a slur about it. The stalling follows an outsider's reaction.
Ambivalent members restrict their calls to acquaintances outside daily life and agonise about exploiting close ties. Footnote 16 has the author's own enthusiasm sagging around critical colleagues.
Disidentified former members made sense of their experience with confidants who were firmly negative. The valence of the outcome matches the valence of the audience.

what_it_would_take_to_cohere.observation: For each informant, a record of whom they approached first, how those people responded, and whether any joined, compared across the four identification types. The reading holds if positively identified members disproportionately had early recruits or tolerant intimates, and ambivalent or disidentified ones had refusals from people they would not give up. The paper prints individual episodes but no such tally. Its non-member interviews are not matched to the distributors who approached them, beyond noting that the first fifteen interviews included failed recruits from one family tree (p. 461).

strains_against.why: The paper argues that either response from intimates, joining or refusing, confirms the upline's teaching. If rejection can strengthen attachment, outsiders' reactions do not sort outcomes.
A positively identified woman reports that former friends now avoid her and treats it as a lesson about them. She met rejection and did not hedge.
The sibling example shows the relationship standard being used to discount a hostile relative. The ideology, not the relative, is doing the deciding.
Those who deidentified explain it by lost interest and contentment, with no mention of how others reacted.

readings.who_could_complete_it: The people on a new distributor's first prospect list, such as spouses, siblings, close friends and co-workers, interviewed about what they said and did, alongside a record of which of them signed up.

readings.wager: The paper sets money aside too quickly. What it shows is not that finances are irrelevant but that members cannot or will not reckon them, and that the unreckoned items are precisely what flows up the line: tapes, books, functions, fees. Read this way, positive identification is the state of not having done the sum. Disidentification is the state of having done it and concluded that the warmth was commercial. Inactivity is the cheap holding position of paying only the renewal. The identification types are stances toward a ledger.

evidence.job: No current or former distributor could, or would, state net profit, and they disagreed on whether training materials count as costs. The paper reports this as a surprise and moves on. Here it is the central finding.

The company's own figure for average monthly gross income of an active distributor is very low, and footnote 8 says nearly all actives fall short of high volume. Most members are spending, not earning.
Members pay a joining fee and often pay for books and tapes. The costs are structural.
Mentors direct which books to read and tapes to buy. The sensegiver is also the person steering purchases.
Disidentified members reinterpret upline kindness as a means to the upline's own income and feel used. Their turn is an economic re-reading of the relationship.
One former member recalls paying the entry sum as [6 words of Pratt (2000), p. 479] pressured pitch. His grievance begins with a payment.
Inactive distributors are defined as those who renew annually but do little else. Every former distributor interviewed had left within a year, roughly when a first annual reckoning would fall due.

what_it_would_take_to_cohere.observation: A per-informant account of money in and money out, including spending on materials and functions and to whom it was paid, set against identification type, together with whether and when each person actually worked out their net position. The reading holds if those who turned against Amway had done the calculation and those who remained devoted had not. The paper says outright that it could not obtain clear figures (p. 463).

strains_against.why: The author met people who quit after reaching high sales levels and devoted actives who were not making money. Financial position, at least in outline, did not line up with attachment.
An inactive distributor who does not buy consistently or recruit still receives unconditional support from his sponsor. Warmth is not visibly conditional on spending.
Those who simply left speak of time, interest and liking their jobs, not of losses.
A stock saying among members is that people come for the money but stay for other people. Members themselves demote the ledger.

readings.who_could_complete_it: Household financial records of current and former distributors, such as receipts for materials and events, order statements and tax filings, or someone like a bookkeeper or tax preparer who has seen such accounts across many members.

readings.wager: The four identification types are stations on a membership career, not separate products of practices succeeding or failing. Entry brings a burst of enthusiasm. The first year brings a crisis in which many leave, indifferent or angry. Survivors either deepen or settle into a long, low-cost stall. The branching diagram is then a cross-section of people caught at different points on one time course, and 'success' and 'failure' of practices name where someone currently stands.

evidence.job: All former distributors interviewed had left within a year, inactive ones had been members for at least a year and a half, and actives ranged up to two decades. Exit clusters early and inactivity appears only after the first year.
A distributor singles out the first few months as the hardest. There is a recognised early trial.
A former distributor describes initial excitement followed by fading interest. This is a sequence within one person, which the paper files as a type.
Among the successful, dreams shift over time from lifestyle to family to saving the country. Positive identification itself has stages.
Footnote 13 notes that members who stop selling are kept in the fold for a long time before being dropped. The organisation treats inactivity as a phase.
Ambivalent members cycle between bursts of activity and long pauses. Their state is described as movement.
The paper states that distributors moved between identification states in several directions but does not discuss this in detail. The trajectories exist in the data and are not printed.

what_it_would_take_to_cohere.observation: Dated trajectories for individual informants, showing which states each passed through and in what order, and whether those now ambivalent or opposed once looked like the devoted. The reading holds if most members share an early sequence and differ mainly in where they stopped. The paper reports that such movements occurred (p. 485) and allows them in its model (p. 482), but prints no individual's sequence apart from fragments of the author's own.

strains_against.why: Tenure ranges of active and inactive distributors overlap heavily. Time in the organisation alone does not separate the devoted from the stalled.
One disidentified man describes humiliation at the recruiting pitch itself. His opposition dates from entry, not from a later stage.
The reported moves run in more than one direction, including from detachment back to devotion. A career implies an order, and these do not obviously have one.
Figure 1 presents the outcomes as alternatives arising from different conditions. The author, who saw the full data, chose branches over a sequence.

readings.who_could_complete_it: A panel of members followed from sign-up with repeated contact over several years, or dated organisational traces, such as renewal records, order histories and function attendance, that show each person's activity over time.
